newsitem.title: USA: U.S. "delighted" by outcome of APEC summit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. "delighted" by outcome of APEC summit.

text.p: U.S. officials said on Monday they were delighted by the outcome of an Asia-Pacific summit and a pledge to press for a global pact to free up information technology trade through the World Trade Organisation.
"We are absolutely delighted with the outcome of this, the 1996 APEC leaders' meeting," U.S.-APEC coordinator John Wolf told reporters after the summit.
"It achieves a number of things which we have been working on for a year."

Leaders of the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum agreed on Monday to call for an information technology agreement substantially reducing tariffs to be concluded by the inaugural WTO meeting in Singapore next month.
The summit also endorsed an action plan for a single Pacific Rim economy by 2020 embracing half of humanity.

U.S. officials said the pact freeing trade in computers, memory chips and telecommunications was due to the direct intervention of President Bill Clinton, who had pitched into a personal lobbying effort with fellow heads of government on the eve of the summit.
"In most of his meetings yesterday he raised the importance of the issue," Wolf said. Clinton arrived late on Saturday and had bilateral talks with the leaders of China, Japan and South Korea.
The agreement would aim to "substantially eliminate tariffs by the year 2000," the summit declared.
The Americans -- the main proponents of an agreement governing a trade that Washington estimates is worth at least $500 billion a year -- wanted APEC's endorsement for zero tariffs.
Although the summit declaration did not cite zero tariffs as the eventual goal of any information technology pact, U.S. officials apparently felt the wording was just as satisfactory.
"Substantially eliminate is tradespeak for zero," said U.S. Trade Representative spokesman Jay Ziegler.

Monday's agreement was also a significant improvement, in American eyes, over the stand taken last week by APEC trade and foreign ministers that merely pushed the issue to the WTO and mentioned no time frame.
